I'm currently using AngularJS in my work and personal projects. There's a reason why its one of the most used frameworks at hackathons.

Pros:

  • Scales and modularizes well.

  • Well supported. Lots of modules/plugins written for it.

  • It's written in full JavaScript, no special syntax (other than templating). Thus, also support for Typescript, ES6, and CoffeeScript.

Cons:

  • Somewhat steep learning curve, difficult for adding new devs onto an existing project

  • As of currently, 2.0 is a pretty looming issue for the community. Porting over is going to be interesting. If you learn Angular 1.x now, you'll have to forget most of it and learn 2.x anyways.
